source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #288 (branch fix/144-tracing-diagnostics at head 9d9e82540ffbff386889f1c98d2052383409ce48 — branch commits cf6848e (stop erasing release tracing; publish a diagnostics event contract (#144)) and 39cdc18 (keep the JIT compile-trace stderr cap from suppressing structured events) plus merge commit 9d9e825 bringing in current main 1253c75, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45250727398 and 45250749786 against the branch and pull-request run 45250703545, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #288 (#144, telomere's tracing dependency carried release_max_level_off, which statically disabled release tracing for the embedder's whole dependency graph; the feature is removed and the runtime diagnostics are published as structured tracing events on the documented telomere::trap / telomere::jit / telomere::stack targets). The branch merged current main (1253c75, containing PR #284) before measurement; the merge was conflict-free. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (1253c75) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45250773315, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR's own. The deltas are the disclosed cost of the fix: with the max-level feature gone, the tracing callsites that were statically erased from release builds exist again. In release, every configuration that links the telomere library grows — stripped file +90,336 B (core) to +152,368 B (wasi-threads), stripped .text +52,752 B (core-nosimd) to +101,200 B (wasi-threads) — while the baseline configuration, which links no telomere code, is byte-identical in both profiles. In release-size the size optimizer still eliminates most of the unused callsite machinery: the core configurations shrink slightly (stripped file −1,856 B to −1,104 B), component and wasi grow by +272 B stripped file (+64 B and +80 B stripped .text), and wasi-threads grows by +192 B stripped file with stripped .text unchanged. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +9.50% (2,433,656 B to 2,664,760 B), up from +5.47%; the release-size component stripped .text series moves from +5.47% to +5.48% (1,169,031 B to 1,233,047 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
